verses.english: Numbered Discourses 10.54
6. Your Own Mind
Serenity

verses.pali: “No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paracittapariyāyakusalo hoti, atha ‘sacittapariyāyakusalo bhavissāmī’ti—
verses.english: “Mendicants, if a mendicant isn’t skilled in encompassing another’s mind, then they should train themselves: ‘I will be skilled in encompassing my own mind.’
And how is a mendicant skilled in encompassing their own mind?

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko ādāse vā parisuddhe pariyodāte acche vā udapatte sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno sace tattha passati rajaṁ vā aṅgaṇaṁ vā, tasseva rajassa vā aṅgaṇassa vā pahānāya vāyamati.
verses.english: Suppose there was a woman or man who was young, youthful, and fond of adornments, and they check their own reflection in a clean bright mirror or a clear bowl of water. If they see any dirt or blemish there, they’d try to remove it.

verses.pali: No ce tattha passati rajaṁ vā aṅgaṇaṁ vā, tenevattamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo:
verses.english: But if they don’t see any dirt or blemish there, they’re happy with that, as they’ve got all they wished for:
‘How fortunate that I’m clean!’

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno paccavekkhaṇā bahukārā hoti kusalesu dhammesu:
verses.english: In the same way, checking is very helpful for a mendicant’s skillful qualities.

verses.pali: ‘lābhī nu khomhi ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa, na nu khomhi lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa, lābhī nu khomhi adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, na nu khomhi lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāyā’ti.
verses.english: ‘Do I have internal serenity of heart or not? Do I have the higher wisdom of discernment of principles or not?’

verses.pali: Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: Suppose that, upon checking, a mendicant knows this:

verses.pali: ‘lābhīmhi ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa, na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāyā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā ajjhattaṁ cetosamathe patiṭṭhāya adhipaññādhammavipassanāya yogo karaṇīyo.
verses.english: ‘I have serenity but not discernment.’ Grounded on serenity, they should practice meditation to get discernment.

verses.pali: So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.
verses.english: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

verses.pali: Sace pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: But suppose that, upon checking, a mendicant knows this:

verses.pali: ‘lābhīmhi adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, na lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā adhipaññādhammavipassanāya patiṭṭhāya ajjhattaṁ cetosamathe yogo karaṇīyo.
verses.english: ‘I have discernment but not serenity.’ Grounded on discernment, they should practice meditation to get serenity.

verses.pali: So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti adhipaññādhammavipassanāya lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa.
verses.english: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

verses.pali: Sace pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: But suppose that, upon checking, a mendicant knows this:

verses.pali: ‘na lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa, na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāyā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṁyeva kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ paṭilābhāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṁ.
verses.english: ‘I have neither serenity nor discernment.’ In order to get those skillful qualities, they should apply extraordinary enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ādittacelo vā ādittasīso vā.
verses.english: Suppose your clothes or head were on fire. In order to extinguish it, you’d apply intense enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

verses.pali: Tasseva celassa vā sīsassa vā nibbāpanāya adhimattaṁ chandañca vāyāmañca ussāhañca ussoḷhiñca appaṭivāniñca satiñca sampajaññañca kareyya.
Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tena bhikkhunā tesaṁyeva kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ paṭilābhāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṁ.
verses.english: In the same way, in order to get those skillful qualities, that mendicant should apply extraordinary enthusiasm …

verses.pali: So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.
verses.english: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

verses.pali: Sace pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṁ jānāti:
verses.english: But suppose that, upon checking, a mendicant knows this:

verses.pali: ‘lābhīmhi ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa, lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāyā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesuyeva kusalesu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya uttari āsavānaṁ khayāya yogo karaṇīyo.
verses.english: ‘I have both serenity and discernment.’ Grounded on those skillful qualities, they should practice meditation further to end the defilements.
I say that there are two kinds of robes:
those you should wear, and those you shouldn’t wear.
I say that there are two kinds of almsfood:
that which you should eat, and that which you shouldn’t eat.
I say that there are two kinds of lodging:
those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.
I say that there are two kinds of village or town:
those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.
I say that there are two kinds of country:
those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.
I say that there are two kinds of individual:
those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.
‘I say that there are two kinds of robes:
those you should wear, and those you shouldn’t wear.’

verses.pali: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
verses.english: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?
Well, should you know of a robe:

verses.pali: ‘idaṁ kho me cīvaraṁ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpaṁ cīvaraṁ na sevitabbaṁ.
verses.english: ‘When I wear this robe, unskillful qualities grow, and skillful qualities decline.’ You should not wear that kind of robe.
Whereas, should you know of a robe:

verses.pali: ‘idaṁ kho me cīvaraṁ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpaṁ cīvaraṁ sevitabbaṁ.
verses.english: ‘When I wear this robe, unskillful qualities decline, and skillful qualities grow.’ You should wear that kind of robe.
‘I say that there are two kinds of robes:
those you should wear, and those you shouldn’t wear.’

verses.pali: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ, idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
